1.note: Also the place name Beth-haccherem (Jer 6:1, Neh 3:14), "house of the vineyards".

2.note: The edition points רֹק, "spittle". An unpointed reading רַק, "only", is also possible: "only her mouth is the wine".

3.note: Literally "standing on a pillar (station)". The sense is uncertain: perhaps "standing in his place", apart from the young men.

4.note: A sound play: צִיר is "envoy" (Prov 25:13) and also "pang"; צֳרִי is "balm".

5.note: Read as חֲלִי, "jewel" (Prov 25:12, Song 7:2). The same letters can mean "its sickness", a hidden barb.

6.note: Read as מִכְסָה, "measure, amount" (Exod 12:4). A reading "its covering" (מִכְסֶה) is also possible.

7.note: רֻקּוֹ is read as "its spittle", as in the first block; perhaps simply "its juice".

8.note: Read as "the ensnared" (from נקש, Ps 9:17). Perhaps "the hard ones", as a pair with קָשִׁים two lines below.

9.note: Topheth, the place of fire (Isa 30:33): the wine's look is fiery. It rhymes with נֹפֶת, "honeycomb", in the next line.

10.note: Literally "and to Eden its shadows". The sense is uncertain.

11.note: בְּדֹלַח is bdellium or crystal (Gen 2:12, Num 11:7); בָּרֶקֶת is a gem of the breastplate (Exod 28:17), often "emerald". The red wine in the clear glass is meant.

12.note: דָּמִים is both "blood" and "price": "dear is her price". "The blood of my liver" follows the pointing כְּבֵדִי; the liver was held to make the blood.

13.note: The same words end the first line of the first poem, there "grow red". Here, against זַכָּה "pure", they mean "foam, grow turbid" (Ps 46:4, 75:9).

14.note: Literally "my soul oppressed (robbed) in his hand": he left and took the narrator's heart with him. The image is uncertain.
